newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot LPGs propped up by NYMEX gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot LPGs propped up by NYMEX gains.

text.p: Spot U.S. liquefied petroleum gas prices were saved from drifting lower in quiet trade midday on Monday by strength in NYMEX futures, players said.
NYMEX crude oil and gasoline were up amid reports linking Iran to the 1996 bombing of U.S. barracks in Saudi Arabia and short covering in gasoline ahead of its seasonal rally.
"Strength in crude is keeping our prices from drfiting," said a Houston-based international broker.
In light activity, spot propane in the U.S. Gulf Coast traded at 34.25 cents and 35.50 cents a gallon, largely unchanged except for buyers being up a quarter cent.
In the Midwest, spot material was 34.25/34.75 cents, with a 5,000-barrel deal done at 34.50 cents.
The butane markets were also quiet and unchanged. There was little news on imports and exports in the U.S. Gulf Coast of the material.
"It was very quiet today. Only a couple of deals have been done," said a Midwest player.
